paper_title: Efficient Ensemble for Fine-tuning Language Models on Multiple Datasets
caption: We show the empirical generalization errors (termed Error in the figures) and estimated Hessian traces of the loss for fine-tuned adapters (using QAdapter on Llama-3-8B) across various hidden dimensions. Smaller adapters achieve the lowest generalization errors. Additionally, the Hessian trace values correlate with generalization errors, suggesting that smaller adapters tend to converge to flatter minima.
model_annotation: This plot illustrates the relationship between Rank and Traces multiplied by 10 to the power of -5, represented in RTE units. The x-axis is labeled “Rank” and has a linear scale ranging from 4 to 256, with tick labels at intervals of 4, 16, 64, and 256. The y-axis is a linear scale representing values from 0.0 to 8.0. A single black solid line with orange square markers is plotted on the graph; starting at a value of approximately 3.2 when Rank is 4, the line decreases to a value of 2.5 at Rank 16, then increases to a value of approximately 4.4 at Rank 64, and finally reaches approximately 6.4 when Rank is 256. Error bars, represented by horizontal black lines, are present at each data point, visually indicating the range of variation around each y-value.
